samples.summary: New `readOnly` gate in YorkieStore (presence seed, updateSelection, ensureAxisOrder) has no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff adds three write suppressions in `YorkieStore`: the constructor's `p.set({activeTabId})` seed, `updateSelection()` and `ensureAxisOrder()`. `sheet-view.tsx` now passes `new YorkieStore(doc, tabId, readOnly)`. Nothing tests any of them: `rg readOnly packages/frontend/tests` returns only docs/pdf/shared-header hits, and `packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-axis-order.test.ts:60` constructs `new YorkieStore(doc as never, tabId)` with no third argument, so every `ensureAxisOrder` case (lines 73–117) exercises only the writable path. The parameter defaults to `false`, so a regression that drops the flag (e.g. `sheet-view` forgetting to pass it, or the guard being placed after the `doc.update`) leaves the whole existing suite green while a share-link viewer either writes `rowOrder`/`colOrder` into the CRDT root or has their sync denied on the first arrow key. The existing axis-order test file already has a doc harness, so a `readOnly` variant is cheap.

samples.summary: YorkieDocStore's new `readOnly` presence gate is untested, including the documented promise that caret anchoring still runs
samples.evidence: Two new early returns are added — `publishResolvedLocalCursor` (line 1263) and `updateCursorPos` (the `if (this.readOnly) return;` after the anchor assignments) — and `docs-view.tsx` now passes `new YorkieDocStore(doc, Boolean(readOnly))`. `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` has an extensive presence suite (lines 359–565 all drive `updateCursorPos` and assert presence), but every store there is built with the one-arg constructor, and `rg readOnly packages/frontend/tests` shows no read-only case anywhere. In particular the field's own doc comment claims the gate 'suppresses the presence write only, never the caret anchoring… so a viewer's caret and selection stay where they were across a peer's edit' — that is exactly the property an early return placed one line too high would break, and no test asserts that `localCursorAnchor`/`localSelectionAnchor` are still populated (or that `resolveAnchoredLocalCursor` still resolves) on a read-only store. The failure is silent: a viewer's caret jumps on every remote edit, or presence is published and the viewer's sync is denied.

samples.summary: The `initialRoot` half of the pdf read-only change got a test; the `onActivePageChange` presence guard did not
samples.evidence: `pdf-collab-provider.test.tsx` (new) pins `initialRoot` for both roles, but the sibling change in the same diff — `if (readOnly || !doc || pageIndex === lastPageRef.current) return;` in `PdfCollabStateProvider.onActivePageChange` — has no coverage. `rg 'onActivePageChange|activePage' packages/frontend` matches only `pdf-collab.tsx`, `pdf-viewer.tsx`, `types/users.ts` and `yorkie-store.ts`; the existing `packages/frontend/tests/app/files/pdf-collab.test.tsx` mounts only with `readOnly={false}` (line 70). If the guard regresses, a viewer scrolling a page issues a `doc.update()` and (per the change's own reasoning) wedges their sync — a user-visible break with nothing to catch it.

samples.summary: The new read-only presence guards in slides-view (`broadcast`) and board-view (`onSelectionChange`) have no test
samples.evidence: Both files gain a one-line `if (readOnlyMount) return;` / `if (readOnly) return;` at the top of a presence publisher. `rg readOnly packages/frontend/tests` shows no slides- or board-view read-only test, and the presence publishers are internal closures created inside a mount effect, so nothing in the suite can observe them. Same failure mode as the other presence gates (a viewer clicking a slide/element wedges their own sync); graded minor because these are the least data-affecting of the set and the guard is a single literal early return.

samples.summary: The missing-secret branches of the service-token helpers (`injector === undefined`, warn) are untested, and `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` has no test at all
samples.evidence: `yorkieServiceTokenInjector` returns `undefined` when the secret is absent, `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` warns and returns `undefined`, and `YorkieService`'s constructor warns when `JWT_SECRET` is unset. There is no `yorkie-service-token.spec.ts` (glob over `packages/backend/src/yorkie/*` shows none) and `rg 'yorkieServiceTokenInjector|signYorkieServiceToken' packages/backend` finds tests only in `auth.service.spec.ts` (always with a literal secret) and `yorkie.service.spec.ts` (config always returns `JWT_SECRET`). So the un-secreted path — the one every ops script and every bare-config test instance takes — is entirely unexercised, including `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv`, which is the only entry point the three migration/copy scripts use.

samples.summary: `sideTokenInjector`'s deliberate no-fallback rule (never this process's JWT_SECRET, never the other side's) has no test
samples.evidence: The new helper is documented as a security-relevant invariant: 'No fallback between the sides, and none to this process's own JWT_SECRET', to avoid sending deployment A's all-documents credential to deployment B. Nothing asserts it: `glob packages/backend/scripts/**/*.spec.ts` returns no files, and the function is module-private in a CLI script with a top-level `main()`. A future edit adding `?? process.env.JWT_SECRET` — the exact mistake the comment warns about — would be caught by no lane. Graded minor only because the script is operator-run and the helper is not on any request path.

samples.summary: `setLocalSelection` neutering is called but not asserted — the test's assertions hold whether or not it forwards
samples.evidence: In `it('neuters every write path')` the body calls `view.setLocalSelection(1, 2)` and then asserts only `store.getText() === 'hello'` and `store.canUndo() === false`. `MemNoteStore.setLocalSelection` (memory.ts:204) mutates only the private `currentSelection` and touches neither text nor the undo stack, so both assertions pass identically if the proxy forwarded the call. Since the wrapper's whole purpose is that a viewer publishes no presence — and `setLocalSelection` is the presence write singled out in `read-only.ts`'s own comment — that member is effectively uncovered. A spy on `store.setLocalSelection` (or reading it through the store's own undo restore point) would make the assertion real.

samples.summary: The divider resize changes (25px hit area, `touch-action: none`, new `track` ratio math) have no test
samples.evidence: The diff changes the split divider from a 7px band to a 25px hit area, adds `touchAction = 'none'` (described as the reason touch drag never reached the resize handler at all), and changes the drag ratio denominator from `rect.width` to `rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`. `rg 'divider|splitRatio|col-resize|touchAction' packages/notes --glob '*.test.ts'` returns nothing, and `editor.test.ts`'s new cases cover only read-only writes and remote application. The style properties are directly assertable in jsdom even if the pointer geometry is not; as shipped, a regression that drops `touch-action` silently returns mobile users to a split they cannot resize.

`yorkieServiceTokenInjector('access-secret')` is called with a non-empty literal secret, so the only branch that can return `undefined` is unreachable in this test; the assertion holds regardless of the behavior under test. The meaningful assertion is the `verifyYorkieToken` round-trip on the next line. Harmless, but it reads as coverage of the `undefined`-secret contract that is in fact untested (see the separate finding on `yorkie-service-token.ts`).

samples.summary: `notes-view`'s new `readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(raw) : raw` wrapping is not tested at the frontend layer
samples.evidence: The new `shared-notes-layout.test.tsx` mocks `@/app/notes/notes-view` away entirely (`vi.mock('@/app/notes/notes-view', …)` returning a stub div), so it asserts only that `readOnly: true` is passed as a prop — the store-wrapping decision inside `NotesView` is never executed by any test. `rg readOnlyNoteStore packages/frontend` matches only `notes-view.tsx` and `shared-notes-layout*`. The engine's `initialize()` also wraps (and `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.test.ts` covers the wrapper itself), so the guarantee survives if this call is dropped — which is why I grade it minor rather than major — but the frontend's own layer of it is unverified, and the frontend has no `tsc` lane to catch a type-level slip either.

verdict.reason: The readOnly gate exists exactly as described in yorkie-store.ts (constructor presence seed L109-113, updateSelection L651, ensureAxisOrder L689), and no test exercises it. A test could only reach the gate by constructing YorkieStore or mounting SheetView; I enumerated both. All six repo-wide `new YorkieStore(` sites outside production pass only two args (yorkie-axis-order.test.ts:60 and the four tests/helpers files), so readOnly is false everywhere in the suite; repo-wide `yorkie-store` imports show no other test consumers; a `readOnly` grep over the entire tests tree (including *.integration.ts) yields only docs/pdf/shared-header hits; the sole test touching sheet-view mocks it out (document-detail-lakehouse-tab.test.tsx:89). revision-preview.tsx's `readOnly: true` is the sheets-engine MemStore mount, not this flag. Because readOnly defaults to false, a regression that drops the flag leaves the whole suite green while a share-link viewer writes rowOrder/colOrder into the CRDT root or has its sync refused by the auth webhook on mount/first arrow key — a user-visible, guard-weakening gap, hence major.

verdict.reason: The readOnly presence gate is real and untested. yorkie-doc-store.ts:604-608 adds the field/two-arg constructor; the gate fires at :1263 (publishResolvedLocalCursor) and :3199 (updateCursorPos, after the anchor assignments at :3192-3194); docs-view.tsx:364 is the only two-arg construction in the repo. Repo-wide searches for `YorkieDocStore(` show every test and helper builds the one-arg (read-write) store (tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:36, editor-undo-selection.test.ts:102/167/262, editor-step-selection-font-size-undo.test.ts:90, merge-repro.test.ts:55, tests/helpers/two-user-docs-yorkie.ts:111,137), and no test sets the private field. The existing presence suite (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:359-404 and following) drives updateCursorPos and asserts presence IS published — the opposite polarity — so it passes whether or not the gate works. packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts covers the engine-level readOnlyDocStore document mutators, not this presence gate, and there is no e2e or docs-view component test. Nothing asserts presence suppression on a read-only mount, nor the documented promise that localCursorAnchor/localSelectionAnchor still populate and resolveAnchoredLocalCursor still resolves — exactly what an early return one line too high would break. Failure is silent and user-visible (viewer sync wedged by an rw PushPull, or viewer caret jumping on remote edits), so major under the missing-test rubric.
